newsitem.title: USA: Convicted U.S. killer gets a peek at electric chair.
newsitem.headline: Convicted U.S. killer gets a peek at electric chair.

text.p: The man next scheduled to die in Florida's notorious electric chair watched the instrument of his execution put through its paces in a test Monday.

"Old Sparky," as the three-legged electric chair is grimly nicknamed by Floridians, was last used in March, when it sent flames shooting from the head of convicted killer Pedro Medina and filled the execution chamber with the stench of burning flesh.
Doctors said Medina died instantly and state experts blamed the incident on a worn sponge in the chair's skullcap.

Leo Jones, slated to die for the 1981 murder of a Jacksonville police officer, accompanied his attorneys and state officials to Florida State Prison in Starke, where experts hired by Jones' state-appointed attorneys spent nearly two hours examining the 74-year-old device.
They were testing whether it is working properly or could be deemed unconstitutionally cruel.

During Monday's test, Jones showed little emotion as investigators twice ran the chair through its execution cycle, in which 2,000 volts of electricity are sent through cables attached to a metal bowl.
The bowl simulates the headpiece worn by prisoners, said Gene Morris, Florida Department of Corrections spokesman.
Morris said that on a few occasions, Jones spoke softly to his attorneys but made no other statement.

"We tested the chair and it works," Morris said. "We examined every piece of machinery and every apparatus that is involved with the chair from the sponges to the headpiece to the cables and the straps. Everything was in working order."
Jones' attorneys argued that they had had no chance to examine the chair themselves.
In May, the state supreme court sent the case back to the trial judge, who must rule by Aug. 8 on Jones' contention that the chair should be mothballed.
The Supreme Court has set oral arguments for Sept. 8. Jones' execution date has been postponed until at least Sept. 15.
